sources.title: Software Engineering at Google
sources.status_note: Published and available by the verification cutoff.
sources.rights_note: Commercial book. Do not ingest text unless the user separately attests lawful access and permitted private processing.
intended_uses: Create engineering checklists that distinguish working code from sustainable code.
Require time, scale, ownership, and maintenance trade-off analysis.
sources.selection_reason: Selected to counter short-term code generation, local optimization, and missing maintenance trade-offs.
sources.freshness_note: Stable engineering principles; verify changing tools and platform details against current official documentation.

sources.title: Learning Domain-Driven Design
sources.status_note: Published and available by the verification cutoff.
sources.rights_note: Commercial book; catalog metadata only without separate access and processing attestation.
intended_uses: Model the business domain and boundaries before selecting frameworks, schemas, or service topology.
Review architectural choices against domain language and change patterns.
sources.selection_reason: Selected to counter premature framework choice, architecture by default, and data models without domain models.
sources.freshness_note: Use for durable modeling methods; confirm current framework-specific implementation guidance in official docs.

sources.title: Effective Software Testing
sources.status_note: Published and available by the verification cutoff.
sources.rights_note: Commercial ebook terms; no corpus ingestion is authorized by catalog inclusion.
intended_uses: Generate test obligations from preconditions, postconditions, invariants, boundaries, and failure modes before implementation.
Use coverage as a diagnostic rather than proof of correctness.
sources.selection_reason: Selected to counter happy-path-only tests, test-after-implementation behavior, and coverage-as-proof.
sources.freshness_note: Testing principles remain useful; library-specific APIs should come from current official documentation.

sources.title: Practical TLA+
sources.status_note: Published and available by the verification cutoff.
sources.rights_note: Commercial book; retain metadata and user-authored learning notes only.
intended_uses: Escalate high-risk concurrent or stateful designs to explicit state machines and checked invariants.
Verify safety and liveness assumptions before implementation.
sources.selection_reason: Selected to counter implementation-before-specification, concurrency blind spots, and example-only validation.
sources.freshness_note: Core formal-method concepts are stable; verify current TLA+ tooling and syntax in official project documentation.

sources.title: A Science of Concurrent Programs
sources.status_note: Published online before the verification cutoff.
sources.rights_note: The author-hosted copy is stated for personal use; do not redistribute it or build a shared derivative corpus.
intended_uses: Teach design-before-code reasoning for concurrent programs.
Require explicit safety, liveness, fairness, and refinement arguments for high-risk work.
sources.selection_reason: Selected to counter code-as-specification, informal concurrency reasoning, and unproved refinement.
sources.freshness_note: Current 2026 source at the cutoff; pair conceptual study with current TLA+ tooling documentation.

sources.title: Property-Based Testing with PropEr, Erlang, and Elixir
sources.status_note: Published and available by the verification cutoff.
sources.rights_note: Commercial book governed by publisher terms; catalog metadata only.
intended_uses: Turn invariants into generative and state-machine tests.
Check that tests detect seeded defects instead of merely passing current code.
sources.selection_reason: Selected to counter handpicked examples, failure of imagination, and false confidence from test counts.
sources.freshness_note: Concepts generalize beyond the named languages; use current language-specific property-testing docs for implementation.

sources.title: Designing Data-Intensive Applications, 2nd Edition
sources.status_note: Second edition published before the verification cutoff.
sources.rights_note: Commercial book; no source-text ingestion without separate lawful-access and processing attestation.
intended_uses: Require workload, consistency, failure, latency, operability, and build-versus-buy analysis before choosing a datastore or architecture.
Compare alternatives through explicit trade-off records.
sources.selection_reason: Selected to counter tool-first architecture, single-node assumptions, and hidden consistency trade-offs.
sources.freshness_note: Current 2026 edition at the cutoff; still verify vendor capabilities and service limits in current official docs.

sources.title: Designing Distributed Systems, 2nd Edition
sources.status_note: Second edition published and available by the verification cutoff.
sources.rights_note: Commercial book; metadata and original learning artifacts only.
intended_uses: Use named distributed patterns as hypotheses rather than defaults.
Demand workload fit, failure-mode analysis, and operational evidence before adopting a topology.
sources.selection_reason: Selected to counter bespoke-everything design, missing operational patterns, and distributed-failure blindness.
sources.freshness_note: Pattern language remains useful; validate orchestration and cloud implementation details against current official docs.

sources.title: Fundamentals of Data Engineering
sources.status_note: Published and available by the verification cutoff.
sources.rights_note: Commercial book; catalog metadata only unless lawful private processing is separately established.
intended_uses: Frame data work across the complete lifecycle.
Include security, governance, orchestration, reliability, and software-engineering concerns in every pipeline design.
sources.selection_reason: Selected to counter pipeline-as-script thinking, missing lifecycle ownership, and technology chasing.
sources.freshness_note: Use for durable lifecycle framing; verify current service features, connector behavior, and limits in official docs.

sources.title: Web Application Security, 2nd Edition
sources.status_note: Second edition published and available by the verification cutoff.
sources.rights_note: Commercial book; catalog metadata only.
intended_uses: Generate threat-informed negative tests for web and API changes.
Review authentication, authorization, configuration, dependency, and abuse-case risks before release.
sources.selection_reason: Selected to counter happy-path security, framework-default trust, and missing abuse cases.
sources.freshness_note: Attack classes endure, but use current OWASP and vendor advisories for active threats and mitigations.

sources.title: Threat Modeling: Designing for Security
sources.status_note: Published and available by the verification cutoff.
sources.rights_note: Commercial book; retain only bibliographic metadata and independently authored artifacts.
intended_uses: Create pre-implementation threat models containing assets, actors, boundaries, abuse paths, mitigations, and validation tests.
Use risk to prioritize security work.
sources.selection_reason: Selected to counter security-after-code, implicit trust boundaries, and unprioritized risk.
sources.freshness_note: The modeling method is durable; complement it with current threat intelligence and platform guidance.

sources.title: Site Reliability Engineering: How Google Runs Production Systems
sources.status_note: Published and freely readable online by the verification cutoff.
sources.rights_note: The stated CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 terms prohibit derivative adaptations; keep this source metadata-only in the learning corpus.
intended_uses: Add service objectives, rollback, observability, capacity, incident, and toil criteria to implementation proof.
Use the public source for direct reading without adapting its text into the corpus.
sources.selection_reason: Selected to counter works-on-my-machine conclusions, missing operational definitions of done, and unbounded automation.
sources.freshness_note: Foundational but older; pair with current service-specific docs and watch the announced second edition.

sources.title: AI Engineering
sources.status_note: Published and available by the verification cutoff.
sources.rights_note: Commercial book; no ingestion without separate lawful-access and private-processing attestation.
intended_uses: Structure AI work across use-case definition, data, evaluation, architecture, feedback, cost, and maintenance.
Compare models and architectures with task-specific evidence rather than popularity.
sources.selection_reason: Selected to counter prompt-only thinking, model chasing, and demos without evaluation.
sources.freshness_note: Strong near-current system framing; model, API, and serving details remain fast-moving and require official docs.

sources.title: AI Agents in Action, Second Edition
sources.status_note: Second edition published before the verification cutoff.
sources.rights_note: Commercial ebook; metadata-only catalog entry.
intended_uses: Model agents as explicit layers with bounded responsibilities.
Require tool contracts, memory boundaries, evaluation, and deployment controls.
sources.selection_reason: Selected to counter agent-as-prompt implementations, unbounded autonomy, and missing feedback layers.
sources.freshness_note: Current 2026 edition at the cutoff; confirm evolving MCP, A2A, model, and framework behavior in official specifications.

sources.title: Designing Machine Learning Systems
sources.status_note: Published and available by the verification cutoff.
sources.rights_note: Commercial book; metadata and original notes only unless processing rights are separately established.
intended_uses: Connect model choices to product objectives, data changes, deployment constraints, monitoring, and continual-learning decisions.
Require online and operational evidence beyond offline metrics.
sources.selection_reason: Selected to counter metrics without product goals, offline-only validation, and static-model assumptions.
sources.freshness_note: System-design principles are durable; verify current model and MLOps capabilities against official sources.

sources.title: Reliable Machine Learning
sources.status_note: Published and available by the verification cutoff.
sources.rights_note: Commercial book; catalog metadata only.
intended_uses: Apply an SRE lens to machine-learning systems.
Require quality, reliability, privacy, fairness, and operational evidence before release.
sources.selection_reason: Selected to counter accuracy-only definitions, model-centric debugging, and missing reliability ownership.
sources.freshness_note: Reliability framing is durable; update threat, fairness, privacy, and platform details from current authoritative sources.

sources.title: Prompt Engineering for LLMs
sources.status_note: Published and available by the verification cutoff.
sources.rights_note: Commercial book; metadata-only catalog entry.
intended_uses: Improve task framing and context selection.
Keep evaluation and workflow design separate from prompt aesthetics and single-sample impressions.
sources.selection_reason: Selected to counter vague instructions, context dumping, and confidence from one sample.
sources.freshness_note: Prompt tactics drift with model families; validate model-specific guidance against current provider documentation and evals.

sources.title: Practical LLM Evaluation for Production Systems
sources.status_note: Published before the verification cutoff.
sources.rights_note: Commercial book; catalog metadata only.
intended_uses: Build versioned evaluation harnesses covering quality, safety, cost, and reliability.
Evaluate tool traces and slices, validate judges, and gate deployments with regressions and rollback criteria.
sources.selection_reason: Selected to counter self-evaluation bias, one-run proof, final-answer-only scoring, and releases without rollback gates.
sources.freshness_note: Current 2026 source at the cutoff; revalidate judge models, tools, and benchmarks continuously.

sources.title: Laws of UX, 2nd Edition
sources.status_note: Second edition published and available by the verification cutoff.
sources.rights_note: Commercial book; metadata-only catalog entry.
intended_uses: Add human-factors checks to interface decisions.
Treat named UX laws as hypotheses to validate with user evidence, not universal defaults.
sources.selection_reason: Selected to counter developer-centered interfaces, feature density, and unexamined defaults.
sources.freshness_note: Behavioral principles are stable; accessibility standards and platform interaction guidance require current official sources.

sources.title: Continuous Discovery Habits
sources.status_note: Published and available by the verification cutoff; ISBN not asserted because it was not verified on the primary page.
sources.rights_note: Commercial book; catalog metadata only.
intended_uses: Require a desired outcome, current user evidence, an opportunity model, and explicit assumption tests before expensive implementation.
Separate discovery evidence from solution enthusiasm.
sources.selection_reason: Selected to counter solution-first building, synthetic user assumptions, and output-over-outcome behavior.
sources.freshness_note: Discovery habits remain useful; validate market and user evidence freshly for every product decision.

sources.title: Accelerate
sources.status_note: Published and available by the verification cutoff.
sources.rights_note: Commercial book; retain bibliographic metadata and independently authored measurement artifacts.
intended_uses: Measure delivery outcomes and capabilities rather than lines of code or agent activity.
Design improvement experiments around system flow, stability, and feedback.
sources.selection_reason: Selected to counter activity-as-productivity, untested process claims, and local speed over system flow.
sources.freshness_note: Foundational empirical source; use current DORA research for updated definitions and findings.

sources.title: Team Topologies, Second Edition
sources.status_note: Second edition published and available by the verification cutoff.
sources.rights_note: Commercial book; metadata-only catalog entry.
intended_uses: Design human and agent responsibilities around clear ownership and bounded cognitive load.
Choose explicit interaction modes and measure whether they improve flow.
sources.selection_reason: Selected to counter agent sprawl, unclear ownership, and coordination overhead.
sources.freshness_note: Near-current second edition; validate organization-specific assumptions through observed flow and team evidence.

sources.title: Platform Engineering on Kubernetes
sources.status_note: Published and available by the verification cutoff.
sources.rights_note: Commercial ebook; metadata-only catalog entry.
intended_uses: Evaluate platforms through user-facing APIs, cognitive-load reduction, delivery outcomes, and progressive verification.
Treat tools as implementation choices, not the definition of a platform.
sources.selection_reason: Selected to counter tool collections presented as platforms, golden paths without user needs, and manual delivery.
sources.freshness_note: Kubernetes and ecosystem details drift quickly; use current project and provider documentation for implementation.

sources.title: The Software Engineer's Guidebook
sources.status_note: Published and available by the verification cutoff.
sources.rights_note: Commercial self-published book; catalog metadata only.
intended_uses: Map learning and work evidence to realistic role expectations.
Keep resume seniority grounded in demonstrated scope and outcomes rather than reading alone.
sources.selection_reason: Selected to counter skill lists without level, technical work without impact, and role inflation.
sources.freshness_note: Career ladders vary by employer; treat the source as a comparison frame and verify target-role expectations from current job evidence.

sources.title: The Tech Resume Inside Out
sources.status_note: Published and available by the verification cutoff; no ISBN asserted from the verified primary source.
sources.rights_note: Individual commercial license with conditional complimentary access; do not ingest or redistribute the book.
intended_uses: Improve evidence selection, relevance, and scanability.
Require every resume claim to be truthful, role-relevant, and independently supportable.
sources.selection_reason: Selected to counter keyword stuffing, unverifiable claims, hard-to-scan resumes, and generic positioning.
sources.freshness_note: Resume mechanics are relatively stable, but hiring signals and role terminology must be checked against current target postings.

sources.title: European Skills, Competences, Qualifications and Occupations (ESCO) v1.2.1
authors: European Commission, DG Employment, Social Affairs and Inclusion
sources.status_note: Released dataset available by the verification cutoff.
sources.rights_note: European Commission reuse is permitted subject to the stated acknowledgement, attribution, non-endorsement, and other reuse conditions.
intended_uses: Use stable concept URIs as the multilingual bridge among learning objectives, job requirements, and resume evidence.
Normalize free-text skills while preserving source labels and mappings.
sources.selection_reason: Selected as the primary multilingual occupation-skill graph and to counter free-text skill drift and resume-learning mismatches.
sources.freshness_note: Pin all identifiers to ESCO v1.2.1 and monitor official version notices before remapping.

sources.title: O*NET 30.3 Database
authors: U.S. Department of Labor, Employment and Training Administration
sources.status_note: Released database available by the verification cutoff.
sources.rights_note: CC BY 4.0 reuse is permitted subject to O*NET and U.S. Department of Labor attribution, change indication, trademark rules, and documented exceptions.
intended_uses: Add occupational importance, level, task, and work-activity structure to ESCO-linked learning and resume evidence.
Use ratings to prioritize learning gaps without treating taxonomy presence as proof of personal skill.
sources.selection_reason: Selected to counter unweighted skill lists, ambiguous role titles, and missing task context.
sources.freshness_note: Pin mappings and attribution to O*NET 30.3; review successor database releases before updating identifiers or ratings.

sources.title: NICE Workforce Framework for Cybersecurity Components v2.0.0
sources.publisher_or_owner: National Institute of Standards and Technology
sources.status_note: Released framework components available by the verification cutoff.
sources.rights_note: NIST-authored public information may be reused with source credit; inspect every component for third-party notices and preserve official identifiers.
intended_uses: Map security learning and evidence to explicit work roles and task-knowledge-skill statements.
Use identifiers as taxonomy links, never as proof that the user performed the work.
sources.selection_reason: Selected to counter vague security skills, courses detached from job tasks, and generic security resume claims.
sources.freshness_note: Pin records to NICE Components v2.0.0 and check NIST release notices and component-level third-party terms before reuse.

sources.title: DigComp 3.0: The Digital Competence Framework for Citizens
sources.status_note: Released framework available by the verification cutoff.
sources.rights_note: CC BY 4.0 and European Commission reuse conditions permit adaptation with attribution, change disclosure, and no implied endorsement.
intended_uses: Add proficiency-aware digital and AI literacy outcomes to occupation-specific mappings.
Separate tool familiarity from demonstrated competence and critical use.
sources.selection_reason: Selected to counter tool-use-as-competence, missing proficiency levels, and uncritical AI use.
sources.freshness_note: Pin outcomes to DigComp 3.0 and monitor official JRC updates before changing competence mappings.

sources.status_note: Early-access and unfinished at the 2026-07-25 verification cutoff; expected after the cutoff.
